conclusions.passage_yes: The claimed 11/11 passage:yes-as-reader result does not hold. On my blind rejudge, only 7 of the 11 are defensibly reader-side; 4 are uncertain because the packet conflicts with or does not cleanly support the reference answer.
conclusions.passage_no: Of the 17 original passage:no cases, I judge 8 reader, 8 passage, and 1 uncertain. So this bucket does not 'dissolve,' but it also is not mostly true passage miss.
conclusions.selector_headroom: These 28 cases justify some selector/packing headroom, but not a clean global estimate. Within this slice, true packet absence is real and non-trivial, yet a large share of misses are still answer-time failures: temporal ordering/arithmetic, scope control in aggregation, and question comprehension.
conclusions.temporal_status: Temporal/status failures remain the strongest reader-side cluster. Several misses come from ordering relative events, converting relative dates, or mishandling conflicting versions without status resolution. Some cases also expose reference/packet inconsistencies rather than pure model failure.
conclusions.limitations: This audit is only over the 28 hand-selected cases from the snapshot. The 26 indeterminate census cases remain outside scope, so nothing here is a global ceiling on selector gains or on overall LongMemEval failure modes.
